chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Jallab, from one of our companions, who said:
A man complained to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about vitiligo (al-Bahiq), so he (peace be upon him) ordered him to cook mung beans, to eat them, and to include them in his food.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, a title for Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْبَهَقَ: Vitiligo, a skin condition characterized by loss of color in patches of the skin.
key_terms.الْمَاشَ: Mung beans, a type of legume used here as a medicinal food.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended treatment for vitiligo according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) prescribes mung beans (*al-mash*) as a specific dietary remedy for vitiligo, illustrating the Shia tradition of linking prophetic medicine (*al-tibb al-nabawi*) with practical daily life. The instruction to cook and incorporate the beans into regular meals highlights the holistic approach to healing in Imami scholarship, where food is viewed not merely as sustenance but as a therapeutic agent. This specific remedy underscores the continuity of medical knowledge transmitted through the Imams, emphasizing natural remedies rooted in the Sunnah.
